age.evidence: Mice were received when they were approximately 8 weeks old.

sex.evidence: Male DBA/2J and C57BL/6J mice were purchased from Jackson Laboratories

dosing.evidence: intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection of vehicle (5% DMSO in sterile deionized water) or test drug. Five minutes later the DOI was administered ... DOI (5 mg/kg) ... administered every other day (48 h) or on a weekly basis

group_housing.evidence: Mice were housed at ≤5 animals per cage with unlimited access to food and fresh water.

assays.assay_description: Mice placed individually in an open-ended Plexiglas cylinder (21 × 34 cm) with a clean paper towel floor, habituated 15 min, injected i.p. with vehicle/test drug, then 5 min later with DOI. Head twitches were counted visually by two observers in 5-min intervals over 30 min (or 2 h in some experiments). Tested across multiple dosing regimens (daily, every-other-day, weekly) and with multiple D2-like antagonists.

application_type.evidence: intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection of vehicle ... DOI was administered

setup_habituation.evidence: Animals were allowed to habituate to the cylinder for 15 min prior to the intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection

setup_restrain.evidence: placed individually in an open ended Plexiglas cylinder

food_restriction.evidence: Testing apparatus is a Plexiglas cylinder with a paper towel floor; no food in apparatus during recording

water_restriction.evidence: No water present in the testing cylinder during recording

time_to_assay.evidence: Five minutes later the DOI was administered and returned to the cylinder ... head twitches started at approximately 90 s after DOI injection

sample_size.evidence: n = 6 (Fig 1); n = 4 (1 mg/kg, Fig 2); n = 9 (Fig 3A); n = 6 (Fig 3B); n = 7 (Fig 4); n = 6 (Fig 5); n = 8 (Fig 6)

outcomes.summary: DOI dose-dependently increased head-twitch frequency in DBA/2J mice (5 mg/kg > 1 mg/kg), with DBA/2J showing significantly more HTRs than C57BL/6J. Daily dosing produced tolerance, while every-other-day or weekly dosing did not. D2-like antagonists (haloperidol, pimozide, benperidol, N-methylbenperidol, SV 293, SV-III-130s) significantly attenuated DOI-induced HTR; eticlopride did not.
outcomes.statistics: Strain p<0.001; tolerance F(6,48)=55.3, p<0.0001; antagonist effect F(3.037,15.9)=18.62, p<0.0001; benperidol F(5,25)=47.5, p<0.0001; N-methylbenperidol F(5,25)=8.08, p<0.0001; haloperidol F(5,25)=14.7, p<0.0001; pimozide F(5,47)=3.03, p=0.01; SV compounds F(4,30)=16.31, P<0.0001
outcomes.evidence: DBA/2J mice exhibited a significantly higher response compared to C57BL/6J ... intensity and cumulative number of head twitches was found to be greater at the higher dose of DOI ... significant reduction in the number of head twitches observed on each consecutive day

judge_notes: All three candidates identified a single HTR assay; consolidated as one assay per rubric (same paradigm under different drug/dose/regimen conditions = 1 assay).
B1 scored 0 (single measure: head twitch count); gptoss's '2-3' was inconsistent because cumulative vs binned counts are the same measure analyzed differently.
D2 scored 2 (61 min–6 h) because the paper explicitly reports cumulative HTR over a 2 h period.
D3 scored 2 (8–14 days): weekly VC tests across ~5 weeks plus tolerance days 0,1,2,3,4,11,18 yields >7 recording days for this assay.
E3 scored 1 (paper towel floor counted as substrate per rubric — present in apparatus during recording).
Vehicle harmonized to 'DMSO' (5% DMSO in deionized water explicitly stated).
Schedule = 'repeated' since DOI was given on multiple days across dosing protocols.
